title: Changing a live database without a hard cutover

masthead.headline: The hard part is not the new shape. It is the window where both shapes are true.
masthead.lede: This board settles the vocabulary before anyone proposes a plan. Every term below has a specific meaning in this work, and two of them are routinely used to mean each other.

sections.label: The shape
sections.title: Why a schema change is not a deploy.

points.lead: Code and data deploy at different speeds.
points.text: A release rolls out over minutes; a backfill of 40 million rows runs for hours. For that whole window, some readers see the old shape and some the new one.

points.lead: So every step must be safe in both directions.
points.text: A step that only works once every reader has upgraded is a step that cannot be rolled back, and a migration you cannot roll back is one you will finish under pressure.

points.lead: The cost is a longer sequence, not more risk.
points.text: Expand, migrate, contract takes three releases where a hard cutover takes one. Each of the three is individually boring, which is the point.

entries.detail: Writing the same fact to both shapes inside one transaction. If either write fails, both fail. It is what keeps the two shapes from diverging while both exist; it is not a safety net, because it does nothing for rows written before it was switched on.

blocks.title: The rollback document comes first
blocks.lead: Before the expand, not after the contract.
blocks.text: A rollback written after the fact is a description of what you happened to do. Written first, it is a constraint on what the migration is allowed to be — and it is what catches an irreversible step hiding in a release that looked reversible.

items.term: Can we skip the shadow read if the dual write is correct?
items.detail: Only if you already know it is correct, which is what the shadow read is for. It is the cheapest way to find the rows where the two shapes disagree, and in the last two migrations it found some.

items.term: How long can the two shapes coexist?
detail: Indefinitely, technically. In practice the contract step slips and the codebase carries both paths for a year. Put a date on the contract release when you write the expand, and treat it as

detail: No. It runs in batches against the primary with a rate limit, and it is resumable. Measured at

items.term: What if a row changes while the backfill is reading it?
items.detail: The dual write wins. The backfill only fills rows whose new shape is still empty, so a row the application has already written is never overwritten by the batch.
